title: Japan is already here

visual.alt: Paper cranes folded from origami paper

intro: Japan is already in this building.
task: Find one thing from Japan. A word, a snack, a tag.
hint: Try a snack shelf, or a suitcase.

moreInfo.title: Why look here?
moreInfo.text: Airports leak other countries. Snacks, stickers and bags travel ahead of people. The first missing page is that Japan does not start when the wheels go down.

reveal: Stories travel ahead of people. You just caught one.

title: Four witnesses
intro: The chronicle needs faces, not only places.
task: Take one photo of the four of you. Still in Copenhagen.
hint: Ask someone nearby, or use the front camera.
reveal: That picture is page one. Everything after this continues from it.

title: The sun that does not set
intro: The flag is a red circle on white.

question.text: What is the red circle on the flag?

choices.response: Look again. The country’s name is a clue.
Not the moon. Think of morning.

reveal: It is the sun. Nihon means origin of the sun.

title: The city under the city
intro: Tokyo has another city underneath it.
task: Find a way down into shops, not only onto a train. Write the name.
hint: Start at a big station. Follow the food signs down.
reveal: These basements are depachika. Tokyo stacked itself. The sky is optional.

title: A machine that is not thirsty
intro: Most vending machines sell drinks. Some do not.
task: Photograph a machine that sells something you cannot drink.
reveal: The city stays open after the staff go home. The machines keep working.

title: The shop that is not convenient
intro: A konbini is a tiny kitchen that never sleeps.
task: Each of you pick one new thing. Write the four things. Then eat.
hint: Look for rice triangles, egg sandwiches, hot snacks.
reveal: This is how a megacity eats at odd hours. Not a snack stop. A system.

title: The cat that is not waving hello
intro: You will see a cat with one paw up.
exactLocation: A shop door, restaurant or station kiosk
observeWhat: Which paw is up, and what is it doing?

choices.response: It looks like a wave. It is not saying goodbye.
Yes. The paw is calling you in.

reveal: The raised paw is an invitation. It is asking you in, not waving goodbye.

intro: The tallest tower is also a pun.
task: How tall is Tokyo Skytree, in metres? Why that number?
exactLocation: Tickets, signs or the lift at Tokyo Skytree
observeWhat: Find the large patch of forest visible from the tower if you can.
hint: Look on tickets, signs, or the lift.
reveal: 634 metres. In old counting, 6-3-4 can be read Musashi, the old name of this place.

title: What felt like art?
task: What made something feel like art, not just lights? One sentence.
hint: Pick one room. Say why it stayed with you.
reveal: Keep that sentence. Kyoto will ask if it still holds.

title: The messengers

visual.alt: The orange torii tunnel at Fushimi Inari in Kyoto

intro: Inari’s messengers are not dogs. Look at the ears.
task: Find a fox statue holding something. What is in its mouth?
exactLocation: Fox statues by the gates at Fushimi Inari Taisha
observeWhat: Look at the fox in front of you. What is it carrying?
hint: Look at the statues by the gates, not only on the mountain.

moreInfo.title: Kitsune
moreInfo.text: Fox spirits carry messages for Inari, kami of rice and success. A key, a jewel or a rice bale is a gift. Farmers once left the first harvest for them.

reveal: Kitsune. Fox spirits. The key, jewel or rice is a gift from Inari.

title: Who paid for a thousand gates?
intro: The mountain is striped orange because of people.
task: Write who you think paid for the gates.
hint: Read a name on the side of a gate.

storySteps.text: Walk until the gates become a tunnel.
Stop at one gate. There is a name on the wood.

choices.label: The government
choices.response: Not this mountain. The names are private.

choices.label: Families and companies
choices.response: Yes. Each gate is a donated prayer.

reveal: Ordinary people paid. The mountain is a ledger of hope, not a royal monument.

title: Bitter, then sweet
intro: Matcha was monk fuel before it was ice cream.
task: Eat or drink real matcha. Was it bitter, sweet, or both?
hint: Tea, sweets, or ice cream. Say who liked it.
reveal: The sweet exists because the tea is severe. Kyoto still serves both.

title: Has the sentence changed?
intro: You answered this in Tokyo. The artefact reads it back.
task: Has “what felt like art?” changed? Write a new sentence, or write “same”.
hint: You do not have to be clever. True is enough.
reveal: Two rooms. Two nights. The chronicle keeps both sentences.

title: What should be remembered
intro: This is not a game. Sit with what you saw.
task: Each person says one thing to remember. Write one sentence you agree on.
hint: Short is fine. True is better than complete.
reveal: Hiroshima was a city of people. Your sentence is now in the chronicle.
